fields.description_1:
Babylonsafety serves organisations with a safety question but not always a clear service route. Safety work can involve different operational contexts, and broad language about protection or compliance can create more confidence than the evidence supports. The website needed to make service boundaries understandable before visitors reached a contact form.

Practical guidance and credibility information had to support the relevant service rather than appear as generic trust badges. On mobile, decision makers should be able to identify the route and next step without processing long technical blocks. The portfolio story also had to avoid guarantees about safety, compliance or incident prevention. The challenge was to present a serious safety-oriented offer clearly while keeping claims scoped to the information and services that can actually be evidenced.
fields.description_2:
I organised Babylonsafety around distinct safety needs so organisations can identify the relevant service before reading deeper guidance. Practical information and credibility content sit beside the decision they support, which keeps the first route understandable without removing technical detail for people who need it.

Enquiry actions appear after enough context for a useful conversation about the operational situation. I kept wording measured and avoided absolute claims about compliance, protection or risk elimination because those depend on the assignment and environment. On smaller screens, service choices, supporting details and contact actions keep a clear order. The portfolio case now shows how WordPress can structure safety services around real decision points instead of relying on generic reassurance or unsupported performance claims.

fields.description_1:
Webactueel Translate has to manage multilingual WordPress content across places normal translation screens may not cover. Source text can live in posts, Elementor, ACF, menus, widgets, taxonomies, WooCommerce and SEO metadata, while review status and exchange files add complexity. Optional AI translation creates a privacy and quality boundary because generated output still needs editorial review.

Frontend replacement also cannot run blindly on admin, REST, AJAX or sensitive WooCommerce requests. The plugin therefore needed context-aware scanning, explicit review states and controlled publication rather than a promise of automatic multilingual quality. The portfolio story had to make those boundaries visible. The challenge was to centralise discovery, editing, SEO support and optional AI assistance while preserving context, privacy, failure behaviour and human review before translated output becomes trusted.
fields.description_2:
I built Webactueel Translate as a WordPress workflow for language management, content scanning, visual editing, translation tables and CSV or XLIFF exchange. The scanner can inspect public post types, Elementor data, ACF fields, menus, widgets, taxonomies and WooCommerce content where those sources are available. Review states keep generated or imported text separate from accepted publication.

Frontend replacement is limited to normal HTML GET requests and skips sensitive contexts such as admin, REST, AJAX and selected WooCommerce flows. Yoast and Rank Math filters support language-specific metadata, while hreflang and canonical foundations organise multilingual output. Optional AI providers work in small review-first batches. The portfolio case now explains a controlled translation system instead of treating generated text or automatic replacement as inherently safe.

fields.description_1:
SEO Shutterstock focuses on a practical WordPress problem: finding stock images that fit the context of a specific page instead of searching separately and remembering where each asset belongs. Page context, search terms, licensing, downloads and media assignment all happen in one workflow, so an attractive result is not enough. The asset also has to be licensed, valid and suitable for the target field.

The project therefore needed clear separation between discovery, review, licensing and assignment, with permissions around higher-risk actions. Existing usage context should help reduce repeated selections across a larger site. The portfolio story could not imply that a stock image or filename creates ranking gains by itself. The challenge was controlled page-aware image research, not a promise of automatic SEO improvement.
fields.description_2:
I structured SEO Shutterstock as a page-aware image workflow inside WordPress. Administrators begin with page or keyword context, review Shutterstock suggestions and then connect a selected licensed asset to the appropriate WordPress or ACF image location. Search, review, licensing and assignment remain separate steps so external images are never treated as automatically suitable.

Downloads and media imports require valid file information before WordPress stores them, while capability checks protect higher-risk actions. Existing usage information helps reduce repeated choices across larger content sets. I kept the portfolio explanation focused on research and controlled placement rather than ranking claims. The case now shows how contextual stock-image work can fit a WordPress editorial process without suggesting that image selection alone guarantees search visibility, traffic or conversion.

fields.description_1:
DCA Dienstverlening combines regular cleaning, specialist work and drone-based cleaning or inspection. Organisations may arrive with a building type or maintenance problem rather than the exact name of the service they need. If every option is presented with the same priority, the offer becomes harder to scan and quotation requests lose useful context.

The website therefore needed strong grouping between routine cleaning, specialist services and drone work, supported by trust information and practical explanations. On mobile, those routes had to stay clear without a long catalogue. The portfolio story also needed to avoid claims about customer satisfaction, efficiency or results that were not independently measured. The challenge was to make a wide facility-service offer understandable while preserving enough detail for a meaningful quotation request.
fields.description_2:
I organised DCA Dienstverlening around service families that match the questions organisations are likely to bring to the site. Regular cleaning, specialist cleaning and drone-related services have separate routes, while reviews, client logos and working-method information support trust without replacing the explanation of the work.

Quotation and contact actions sit near the sections where a visitor has enough context to describe the location and service need. The same hierarchy remains visible on smaller screens, with service choices and next steps easy to scan. I kept the portfolio wording factual and tied to the offer, avoiding invented claims about lead growth, satisfaction or operational improvement. The case now explains how WordPress makes a broad service range easier to navigate without flattening it into generic cleaning copy.

fields.description_1:
ACF Image Auto Filler reduces repetitive image assignment, but bulk convenience becomes risky when WordPress content contains different ACF structures. A simple Image field can be mapped predictably, while repeaters, flexible content, galleries and clones introduce nested relationships that should not be guessed. Existing values also need protection when an editor does not intend to overwrite them.

The plugin therefore needed a previewable mapping workflow, optional overwrite, manual mapping, batch limits, rollback and an audit trail. The portfolio story had to explain why some field types are deliberately excluded and that content is not sent to external services. The challenge was to make large image assignments faster without sacrificing visibility, permissions or recovery when automatic order is not enough.
fields.description_2:
I built ACF Image Auto Filler around a review-first admin flow. Editors select content, supported fields and Media Library images, then see the proposed mapping before any write. Top-level ACF Image fields are supported, along with Image fields inside Groups when enabled, while featured images can be handled separately.

Existing values are skipped unless overwrite is explicitly enabled. Manual mapping, batch mode and CSV dry-run export provide more control, and saved runs can retain rollback data for the current user. An admin audit log records operations, while capability and per-item permission checks protect bulk changes. Repeaters, flexible content, galleries and clones remain excluded from automatic filling. The portfolio case now explains a bounded image-assignment workflow instead of pretending complex ACF data can be safely guessed.
